name: Can you resurface a pool without replacing the tile or coping?

mainEntity.name: Is it okay to keep the existing waterline tile and coping during a pool resurfacing project?
mainEntity.text: Is it okay to keep the existing waterline tile and coping during a pool resurfacing project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pool resurfacing does not automatically require new tile or coping. If the existing tile is stable and the coping is not cracked or shifting, many homeowners keep them and only replace the interior finish. That said, once the pool is drained and crews are already on site, it is often more efficient to handle tile or coping issues at the same time, especially if the surfaces are chipped, stained, or partially detached. This is common in older Los Angeles-area pools where the finish may be failing while the tile band also shows age. Combining the work can improve the final look and avoid tearing into a newly finished pool later. The tradeoff is cost: adding tile or coping raises the budget. Homeowners should ask whether the current materials are still structurally sound and whether postponing those upgrades would create compatibility or color-matching problems later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, many pools can be resurfaced without replacing tile or coping if those components are still sound. However, damaged, loose, or outdated tile and coping often make sense to replace at the same time because the pool is already drained and work access is open. Matching old materials later can be difficult.
